I am 74 years old, and I have been growing cotton on this land for 55 years. My bones are not what they used to be, and my children and grandchildren have gone to work in the city, so I mostly tend these 2 mu by myself now. But I know every inch of this soil, and I know what cotton needs in Quzhou.

This spring, I will plant cotton across my whole 2 mu. I will buy improved seeds from the village supply store — I have used guoxinmian varieties for years, and they give me reliable bolls. I cannot afford to gamble with unfamiliar seeds at my age. Before sowing in late April, I will rotary-till the field to break up the soil and warm it, then lay plastic mulch to keep the heat in and the weeds down. That is how we grow cotton here.

For fertilizer, I will spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a basal dose before planting — something like 15-15-15 or whatever the shop has this year — and top-dress once when the plants flower. That works out to roughly 15 jin of nitrogen, 10 jin of phosphorus, and 8 jin of potassium per mu. I do not bother weighing it on a scale; I go by the bag and by memory. My plot is small, so I can walk it and see if the leaves look hungry.

Irrigation comes from my well. Water costs diesel and labor, so I will irrigate twice: once before sowing to moisten the soil, and once in mid-summer when the bolls are filling. If the rains come well, two times is enough for 2 mu. Any more and I am just wasting money and wearing out my pump.

Pesticides are the thing I cannot skip. Cotton bollworms come every year like clockwork. I will spray about 10 to 12 times from June through August — whenever I see the first sign of holes in the leaves or sticky eggs. I mix the spray myself and carry the tank on my back. It is heavy work, but losing the crop to worms would be worse.

I expect about 500 jin of seed cotton per mu this year. Last year I got close to that. I am older now, so I do not push for record yields — I aim for steady, decent output that I can sell to the buyer who comes to the village. My family does not rely on this land alone anymore, but I still take pride in doing it right.
